content: 1. A computational simulation model was discussed in a study published in The Lancet Infectious Diseases in 2013, which analyzed specific aspects of infectious diseases. The study is detailed in volume 13, issue 4, pages 342-348. 2. The Pan American Health Organization (PAHO) published a report in 2016 titled Neglected Infectious Diseases in the Americas: Success Stories and Innovation to Reach the Neediest. This document, consisting of 164 pages, highlights efforts to combat neglected diseases in the region. 3. The World Health Organization (WHO) released the second edition of its Handbook for Guideline Development in 2014, which provides a comprehensive framework for creating evidence-based health guidelines. 4. Roberto Salvatella contributed a historical perspective on Chagas disease in a publication by PAHO and the Healthy World Foundation in 2006. This work, titled La Enfermedad de Chagas, a la Puerta de los 100 Años del Conocimiento de una Endemia Americana Ancestral, spans pages 19-22 and reflects on the disease's evolution over a century. 5. The Special Program for Research and Training in Tropical Diseases (TDR) convened a Scientific Working Group on Chagas Disease in Buenos Aires, Argentina, from April 17-20, 2005. The findings were published in a 96-page report by TDR in 2007. 6. Pinto Dias JC conducted a clinical epidemiological review of the indeterminate form of chronic Chagas disease, published in Revista da Sociedade Brasileira de Medicina Tropical in 1989, volume 22, issue 3, pages 147-156. 7. Salvatella R, Irabedra PS, Sánchez D, Castellanos LG, and Espinal M discussed South-South cooperation in addressing Chagas disease in an article published in The Lancet in 2013, volume 382, issue 9890, pages 395-396. 8. The WHO published a report in 2013 on neglected tropical diseases, emphasizing the global burden and strategies for their elimination. 9. PAHO released a document in 2009 titled Elimination of Neglected Diseases and Other Poverty-Related Infections, which outlines strategies for addressing these conditions. 10. PAHO also developed a Strategy and Plan of Action for Chagas Disease Prevention, Control, and Care in 2010, providing guidelines for diagnosis and treatment. 11. In 2016, PAHO published a Plan of Action for the Elimination of Neglected Infectious Diseases and Post-Elimination Actions (2016-2022) during the 158th Session of the Executive Committee in Washington, DC. 12. PAHO released a report in 2015 on the Supply of Blood for Transfusion in Latin American and Caribbean Countries (2012-2013), addressing blood safety and availability. 13. The Drugs for Neglected Diseases initiative (DNDi) provides detailed information on Chagas disease on its website, which was accessed on June 8, 2016. 14. PAHO published a tool in 2018 titled Strengthening National Evidence-Informed Guideline Programs: A Tool for Adapting and Implementing Guidelines in the Americas, aimed at improving health guideline development. 15. Guyatt GH, Oxman AD, Kunz R, et al. published the second installment of the GRADE guidelines in Journal of Clinical Epidemiology in 2011, volume 64, issue 4, pages 395-400. This article focuses on framing clinical questions and determining important outcomes. 16. Guyatt GH, Oxman AD, Santesso N, et al. discussed preparing summary of findings tables for binary outcomes in the 12th installment of the GRADE guidelines, published in Journal of Clinical Epidemiology in 2013, volume 66, issue 2, pages 158-172. 17. Guyatt GH, Thorlund K, Oxman AD, et al. addressed preparing summary of findings tables for continuous outcomes in the 13th installment of the GRADE guidelines, published in Journal of Clinical Epidemiology in 2013, volume 66, issue 2, pages 173-183. 18. Doebler P and Holling H conducted a meta-analysis of diagnostic accuracy using the MADA framework, which was published by the University of Münster. 19. Schünemann H, Brozek J, Guyatt G, Oxman A, et al. edited the Handbook for Grading the Quality of Evidence and the Strength of Recommendations Using the GRADE Approach, updated in October 2013. 20. Hultcrantz M, Rind D, Akl EA, et al. clarified the construct of certainty of evidence in a publication by the GRADE Working Group in Journal of Clinical Epidemiology in 2017, volume 87, pages 4-13. 21. Andrews J, Guyatt G, Oxman AD, et al. discussed the significance and presentation of recommendations in the 14th installment of the GRADE guidelines, published in Journal of Clinical Epidemiology in 2013, volume 66, issue 7, pages 719-725. 22. Andrews JC, Schünemann HJ, Oxman AD, et al. explored determinants of a recommendation's direction and strength in the 15th installment of the GRADE guidelines, published in Journal of Clinical Epidemiology in 2013, volume 66, issue 7, pages 726-735. 23. Moscatelli G, Moroni S, García-Bournissen F, et al. examined the prevention of congenital Chagas disease through treatment of women of childbearing age in a study published in Memórias do Instituto Oswaldo Cruz in 2015, volume 110, issue 4, pages 507-509. 24. Caryn B, Martin DL, and Gilman RH reviewed acute and congenital Chagas disease in Advances in Parasitology in 2011, volume 75, pages 19-47. 25. A multidisciplinary team was established to develop evidence-based guidelines for the diagnosis and treatment of Chagas disease, adhering to the highest methodological standards. This team included experts such as Dr. Roberto Chuit, Dr. Alejandro Luquetti, Dr. Jaime Altcheh, Dr. Faustino Torrico, Dr. Juan Carlos Villar, and Dr. Roberto Salvatella, among others. 26. The guidelines also included a methodological team led by Dr. Ariel Izcovich and Dr. Juan Martín Criniti, who contributed to the rigorous development process. 27. The guidelines addressed key diagnostic and therapeutic questions using the PICO framework, focusing on populations such as adults, children, and women of childbearing age with suspected or confirmed Chagas disease. Various diagnostic assays and therapeutic interventions, including trypanocidal treatments, were evaluated for their efficacy and outcomes.
